drivingQuestion: May two who ate together form a zimmun if they wish, and which of Rav and Rabbi Yoḥanan held that they may not?
outcomeNote: The sugya settles that Rabbi Yoḥanan is the one who held two may not form a zimmun (after the parallel attempt to assign that view to Rav is rejected), meets Rava bar Rav Huna's counter-report and answers it, and rules practically like Mar Zutra that a zimmun of ten requires the absent one's return; the attached questions on amen and on who breaks and who blesses are each resolved in turn.

segments.he: אִתְּמַר: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁאָכְלוּ כְּאַחַת, פְּלִיגִי רַב וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן. חַד אָמַר: אִם רָצוּ לְזַמֵּן — מְזַמְּנִין, וְחַד אָמַר: אִם רָצוּ לְזַמֵּן — אֵין מְזַמְּנִין.
segments.en: The mishna rules that three who ate as one are required to join together and recite Grace after Meals. The Gemara discusses this halakha further: «It was stated: Two who ate as one» and wish to join together in a zimmun, although they are under no obligation, are they permitted to do so?« Rav and Rabbi Yoḥanan disagreed: One said: If they wanted to join together, they may form a zimmun. The other said:» Even «if they wanted to join together, they may not form a zimmun.»

segments.he: תְּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁאָכְלוּ כְּאַחַת חַיָּיבִין לְזַמֵּן. שְׁלֹשָׁה — אִין, שְׁנַיִם — לָא!
segments.en: The Gemara cites a proof from what «we learned» in our mishna: «Three who ate as one are required to join together» and recite Grace after Meals. By inference: «Three, yes,» they form a zimmun; «two, no,» they do not form a zimmun. This contradicts the opinion that holds that two individuals who wish to form a zimmun may do so.

segments.he: הָתָם חוֹבָה, הָכָא רְשׁוּת.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: There is no proof from the mishna, as «there,» the mishna discussed an «obligatory» zimmun; «here,» the amora’im disagree with regard to an «optional» zimmun.

segments.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: שְׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁאָכְלוּ כְּאַחַת — חַיָּיבִין לְזַמֵּן, וְאֵין רַשָּׁאִין לֵיחָלֵק. שְׁלֹשָׁה — אִין, שְׁנַיִם — לָא!
segments.en: The Gemara cites an additional proof. «Come and hear: Three who ate as one are required to join together» and recite Grace after Meals «and may not disperse» to recite Grace after Meals individually. Apparently, «three, yes,» they form a zimmun; «two, no,» they do not form a zimmun. If a zimmun was possible with two people, three people would not be forbidden to disperse, as even if one recited Grace after Meals alone, the remaining two would constitute a zimmun.

segments.he: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּקָבְעוּ לְהוּ בְּחוֹבָה מֵעִיקָּרָא.
segments.en: The Gemara rejects this proof: «It is different there,» in the case of a group of three who dispersed, because «from the outset, they established themselves as» a group of three who were «obligated» to form a zimmun. Consequently, they are not permitted to forego an obligatory zimmun in favor of an optional one.

segments.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַשַּׁמָּשׁ שֶׁהָיָה מְשַׁמֵּשׁ עַל הַשְּׁנַיִם — הֲרֵי זֶה אוֹכֵל עִמָּהֶם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָתְנוּ לוֹ רְשׁוּת. הָיָה מְשַׁמֵּשׁ עַל הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה — הֲרֵי זֶה אֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל עִמָּהֶם, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נָתְנוּ לוֹ רְשׁוּת!
segments.en: The Gemara cites an additional proof. «Come and hear,» based on what was taught in a baraita: «A waiter who was serving two people eats with them, although they did not give him permission» to do so, because he will thereby be eligible to join them in a zimmun. If a waiter «was serving three» people, «he may not eat with them unless they gave him permission» to do so. Evidently, two may not form a zimmun. If that were the case, the waiter would require permission even when serving two people.

segments.he: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «It is different there,»

segments.he: דְּנִיחָא לְהוּ דְּמַקְבַּע לְהוּ בְּחוֹבָה מֵעִיקָּרָא.
segments.en: in the case of a waiter, «because from the outset, they prefer to establish» their zimmun «as an obligation» rather than as an option.

segments.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: נָשִׁים מְזַמְּנוֹת לְעַצְמָן, וַעֲבָדִים מְזַמְּנִים לְעַצְמָן, נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים אִם רָצוּ לְזַמֵּן — אֵין מְזַמְּנִין. וְהָא נָשִׁים אֲפִילּוּ מְאָה וְהָא מְאָה נָשֵׁי כִּתְרֵי גַּבְרֵי דָּמְיָין, וְקָתָנֵי נָשִׁים מְזַמְּנוֹת לְעַצְמָן וַעֲבָדִים מְזַמְּנִין לְעַצְמָן!
segments.en: The Gemara cites yet another proof. «Come and hear: Women form a zimmun for themselves and slaves form a zimmun for themselves;» however, «women, slaves, and minors,» even «if they wish to form a zimmun» together, «they may not form a zimmun. «But aren’t one hundred women» considered «the equivalent of two men,» in that they cannot constitute a prayer quorum? «And» yet, the baraita «teaches» that «women form a zimmun for themselves and »Canaanite« slaves form a zimmun for themselves». Apparently, like women, two men can form a zimmun on their own.»

segments.he: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּאִיכָּא דֵּעוֹת.
segments.en: The Gemara rejects this: «There it is different because,» although women cannot constitute a prayer quorum, since «there are» three individual «minds,» i.e., people, three women can fulfill the verse: “Praise God with me, and we will exalt His name together.” Two men cannot.

segments.he: אִי הָכִי, אֵימָא סֵיפָא: נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים אִם רָצוּ לְזַמֵּן — אֵין מְזַמְּנִין. אַמַּאי לָא, וְהָא אִיכָּא דֵּעוֹת!
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «If so, say the latter clause» of this baraita: «Women and slaves, if they wish to form a zimmun, they may not form a zimmun. Why not? Aren’t» they individual «minds,» which should enable the collective praise of God?

segments.he: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם מִשּׁוּם פְּרִיצוּתָא.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: That is not the reason that women and slaves were prohibited from forming a zimmun together. Rather, «it is different there,» as the Sages were concerned with regard to women and slaves joining together «due to promiscuity.»

segments.he: תִּסְתַּיֵּים, דְּרַב דְּאָמַר אִם רָצוּ לְזַמֵּן — אֵין מְזַמְּנִין. דְּאָמַר רַב דִּימִי בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב: שְׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁאָכְלוּ כְּאַחַת וְיָצָא אֶחָד מֵהֶם לַשּׁוּק — קוֹרְאִין לוֹ וּמְזַמְּנִין עָלָיו. טַעְמָא דְּקוֹרְאִין לוֹ, הָא לֹא קוֹרְאִין לוֹ — לָא!
segments.en: In the dispute between Rav and Rabbi Yoḥanan, it is unclear which amora held which opinion. The Gemara seeks to resolve this: «Conclude that Rav» is the one who «said: If they wanted to join together, they may not form a zimmun. As Rav Dimi bar Yosef said» that «Rav said: Three» people «who ate as one and one of them went out to the marketplace, they call him and include him in the zimmun. The reason is because they call him;» by inference, «if they do not call him, no,» they cannot form a zimmun.

segments.he: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּאִקְּבַעוּ לְהוּ בְּחוֹבָה מֵעִיקָּרָא.
segments.en: The Gemara rejects this proof: «It is different there,» in the case of three who ate together and one of them left, because «from the outset, they established themselves as» a group of three who were «obligated» to form a zimmun. That is why they need to call him and include him in their zimmun.

segments.he: אֶלָּא תִּסְתַּיֵּים, דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הוּא דְּאָמַר אִם רָצוּ לְזַמֵּן — אֵין מְזַמְּנִין, דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁאָכְלוּ כְּאַחַת — אֶחָד מֵהֶן יוֹצֵא בְּבִרְכַּת חֲבֵירוֹ.
segments.en: The Gemara now attempts to prove the opposite: «Rather, conclude that Rabbi Yoḥanan is the one who said: If they wanted to join together, they may not form a zimmun, as Rabba bar bar Ḥana said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Two» people «who ate as one, one fulfills his obligation» to recite a blessing «with the» recitation of the «blessing of the other.»

segments.he: וַהֲוֵינַן בַּהּ: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, תְּנֵינָא: שָׁמַע וְלֹא עָנָה — יָצָא! וְאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵין בִּרְכַּת הַזִּימּוּן בֵּינֵיהֶם. תִּסְתַּיֵּים.
segments.en: The Gemara comments: «And we discussed it» in an attempt to clarify the halakha. «What is he teaching us? We» already «learned this» halakha explicitly: «One who heard» a blessing «and did not respond,» nevertheless «he fulfilled» his obligation «And Rabbi Zeira said:» Rabbi Yoḥanan’s statement teaches us that «there is no blessing of zimmun among them.» Indeed, «conclude» that Rabbi Yoḥanan is the amora who held that two may not form a zimmun.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא לְרַב הוּנָא: וְהָא רַבָּנַן דַּאֲתוֹ מִמַּעְרְבָא אָמְרִי, אִם רָצוּ לְזַמֵּן — מְזַמְּנִין, מַאי לָאו דִּשְׁמִיעַ לְהוּ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן? לָא, דִּשְׁמִיעַ לְהוּ מֵרַב, מִקַּמֵּי דִּנְחֵית לְבָבֶל.
segments.en: With regard to this, «Rava bar Rav Huna said to» his father «Rav Huna: Didn’t the Sages who came from the West,» from Eretz Yisrael, «say that» two individuals who ate together, «if they wanted to join together, they may form a zimmun? What, is it not that they heard» it «from Rabbi Yoḥanan,» who was from Eretz Yisrael? Rav Huna answered: «No,» this is not a proof, as it is possible «that they heard» this halakha «from Rav before he» left Eretz Yisrael and «descended to Babylonia.»

segments.he: גּוּפָא. אָמַר רַב דִּימִי בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב: שְׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁאָכְלוּ כְּאַחַת, וְיָצָא אֶחָד מֵהֶם לַשּׁוּק — קוֹרְאִין לוֹ, וּמְזַמְּנִין עָלָיו. אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: וְהוּא דְּקָרוּ לֵיהּ וְעָנֵי.
segments.en: The Gemara now explains «the matter» of Rav’s statement «itself: Rav Dimi bar Yosef said» that «Rav said: Three» people «who ate as one and one of them went out to the marketplace, they call him and include him in the zimmun,» even if he is not beside them. And «Abaye said: This is» only in a case «that they call him and he responds,» but if he is too far away to answer he cannot be included.

segments.he: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: וְלָא אֲמַרַן, אֶלָּא בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה, אֲבָל בַּעֲשָׂרָה עַד דְּנֵיתֵי.
segments.en: «Mar Zutra said: We only said» this, that it is sufficient to hear and answer, «with regard to» a zimmun of «three; but, with regard to» a quorum of «ten,» they may not form a zimmun which includes mention of God’s name «until» the one who left «comes» and sits with them.

segments.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: אַדְּרַבָּא אִיפְּכָא מִסְתַּבְּרָא תִּשְׁעָה נִרְאִין כַּעֲשָׂרָה, שְׁנַיִם אֵין נִרְאִין כִּשְׁלֹשָׁה.
segments.en: «Rav Ashi strongly objects to this: On the contrary, the opposite is more reasonable. Nine» people who ate together «appear like ten,» so even if one is missing, the quorum does not seem to be incomplete. «Two» people who ate together «do not appear like three,» so it would be reasonable to require the actual presence of the third.

segments.he: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּמָר זוּטְרָא. מַאי טַעְמָא? — כֵּיוָן דְּבָעֵי לְאַדְכּוֹרֵי שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם — בְּצִיר מֵעֲשָׂרָה לָאו אוֹרַח אַרְעָא.
segments.en: The Gemara concludes: «And the halakha is in accordance with» the opinion of «Mar Zutra. «What »is« the reason? Because »in a zimmun of ten «they need to mention the Name of Heaven, »and it is« not proper conduct »to invoke the Name of Heaven with «fewer than ten» people present.»

segments.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: נְקִיטִינַן שְׁנַיִם שֶׁאָכְלוּ כְּאַחַת — מִצְוָה לֵיחָלֵק. תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁאָכְלוּ כְּאַחַת — מִצְוָה לֵיחָלֵק. בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, כְּשֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם סוֹפְרִים, אֲבָל אֶחָד סוֹפֵר וְאֶחָד בּוּר — סוֹפֵר מְבָרֵךְ, וּבוּר יוֹצֵא.
segments.en: With regard to the halakhot of zimmun, «Abaye said» that «we have a tradition: Two» people «who ate as one, it is a mitzva» for them «to separate» and for each to recite a blessing for himself. «This was also taught» in a baraita: «Two» people «who ate as one, it is a mitzva» for them «to separate» The baraita, however, adds: «In what» case «are these matters stated?» Specifically «when both» individuals «are learned people [soferim]» and capable of reciting prayers and blessings. «However,» if «one of them was a learned person and the other an ignoramus, the learned person recites the blessing» and «the ignoramus thereby fulfills» his obligation.

segments.he: אָמַר רָבָא: הָא מִילְּתָא אַמְרִיתָא אֲנָא, וְאִיתַּמְרָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא כְּווֹתִי: שְׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁאָכְלוּ כְּאַחַת, אֶחָד מַפְסִיק לַשְּׁנַיִם, וְאֵין שְׁנַיִם מַפְסִיקִין לָאֶחָד.
segments.en: «Rava said: This is a statement that I said and it was stated in the name of Rabbi Zeira in accordance with my» opinion: «Three» people «who ate as one» but did not conclude their meals together, «one interrupts» his meal in order «to» join the other «two» in a zimmun, «but two do not interrupt» their meal «to» join the other «one» in a zimmun.

segments.he: וְלָא? וְהָא רַב פָּפָּא אַפְסֵיק לֵיהּ לְאַבָּא מָר בְּרֵיהּ אִיהוּ וְחַד! שָׁאנֵי רַב פָּפָּא, דְּלִפְנִים מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין הוּא דַּעֲבַד.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges: «And» do two really «not» interrupt their meal to join the other one in a zimmun? «Didn’t Rav Pappa interrupt» his meal «to» enable «Abba Mar, his son,» to recite the zimmun blessing; and, in that case, it was Rav Pappa «and one» other person? The Gemara responds: The case of «Rav Pappa is different, as» he «acted beyond the letter of the law.»

segments.he: יְהוּדָה בַּר מָרִימָר וּמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי וְרַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי כָּרְכִי רִיפְתָּא בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי, לָא הֲוָה בְּהוּ חַד דַּהֲוָה מוּפְלָג מֵחַבְרֵיהּ לְבָרוֹכֵי לְהוּ. יָתְבִי וְקָא מִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: הָא דִּתְנַן שְׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁאָכְלוּ כְּאַחַת חַיָּיבִין לְזַמֵּן, הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא אָדָם גָּדוֹל, אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּכִי הֲדָדֵי נִינְהוּ — חִלּוּק בְּרָכוֹת עָדִיף.
segments.en: The Gemara relates that three Sages, «Yehuda bar Mareimar, Mar bar Rav Ashi and Rav Aḥa of Difti ate bread together. None among them was greater than the other» in either age or wisdom, rendering him the obvious choice to «recite the blessing on their behalf. They sat down and raised a dilemma: That which we learned» in our mishna: «Three» people «who ate as one are required to join together» and recite Grace after Meals, does «that apply only when there is a great man» among them, «but where they are on a par with each other,» perhaps «separating» and reciting independent «blessings is preferable?»

segments.he: בָּרֵיךְ אִינִישׁ לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ. אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּמָרִימָר. אָמַר לְהוּ: יְדֵי בְּרָכָה יְצָאתֶם, יְדֵי זִימּוּן לֹא יְצָאתֶם. וְכִי תֵּימְרוּ: נֶיהְדַּר וּנְזַמֵּן, אֵין זִימּוּן לְמַפְרֵעַ.
segments.en: Indeed, that is what they did, and «each person recited the blessing for himself.» Later, «they came before Mareimar» to ask him if they had acted correctly. Mareimar «said to them:» Although «you fulfilled your» obligation to recite a «blessing» over your food, «you did not fulfill» your obligation to form a «zimmun. And if you say: Let us go back and form a zimmun, there is no retroactive zimmun.» Once the blessing over the meal has been recited, one can no longer recite the zimmun.

segments.he: בָּא וּמְצָאָן כְּשֶׁהֵן מְבָרְכִים, מַהוּ אוֹמֵר אַחֲרֵיהֶם? רַב זְבִיד אָמַר: ״בָּרוּךְ וּמְבוֹרָךְ״. רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: עוֹנֶה ״אָמֵן״.
segments.en: The Gemara discusses another question: «One who came and found them reciting the» zimmun «blessing, what does he say after them» in response to the zimmun.«Rav Zevid said» that he says: «Blessed» is He «and blessed» is His Name for ever and all time (Tosafot). «Rav Pappa said: He answers amen.»

segments.he: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי, הָא — דְּאַשְׁכְּחִינְהוּ דְּקָא אָמְרִי ״נְבָרֵךְ״, וְהָא — דְּאַשְׁכְּחִינְהוּ דְּקָא אָמְרִי ״בָּרוּךְ״. אַשְׁכְּחִינְהוּ דְּקָא אָמְרִי ״נְבָרֵךְ״ — אוֹמֵר ״בָּרוּךְ וּמְבוֹרָךְ״, אַשְׁכְּחִינְהוּ דְּקָא אָמְרִי ״בָּרוּךְ״ — עוֹנֶה ״אָמֵן״.
segments.en: The Gemara explains that Rav Zevid and Rav Pappa «do not disagree. This is» in a case «where he found them saying: Let us bless; and that is» in a case «where he found them saying: Blessed be.» The Gemara specifies: «Where he found them saying: Let us bless, he says: Blessed» is He «and blessed» is His Name for ever and all time; «where he found them saying: Blessed be, he answers amen.»

segments.he: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: הָעוֹנֶה ״אָמֵן״ אַחַר בִּרְכוֹתָיו — הֲרֵי זֶה מְשׁוּבָּח. וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: הֲרֵי זֶה מְגוּנֶּה.
segments.en: A similar explanation resolves a difficulty in a related topic. «One» baraita «taught: One who answers amen after his» own «blessings, it is praiseworthy. Another» baraita «taught: It is reprehensible.»

segments.he: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא — בְּ״בוֹנֶה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם״. הָא — בִּשְׁאָר בְּרָכוֹת.
segments.en: The Gemara resolves this apparent contradiction: This is «not difficult. This,» where the first baraita says that it is praiseworthy to answer amen after his own blessing, «is in» the blessing: «Who builds Jerusalem; this,» where the second baraita deems it offensive, «is in other blessings.»

segments.he: אַבָּיֵי עָנֵי לֵיהּ בְּקָלָא, כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלִשְׁמְעוּ פּוֹעֲלִים וְלֵיקוּמוּ, דְּ״הַטּוֹב וְהַמֵּטִיב״ לָאו דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא. רַב אָשֵׁי עָנֵי לֵיהּ בִּלְחִישָׁא, כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא נְזַלְזְלוּ בְּ״הַטּוֹב וְהַמֵּטִיב״.
segments.en: The Gemara relates: «Abaye would answer» amen «aloud» after reciting the blessing: Who builds Jerusalem, «so the workers would hear and stand» to return to work, «as» the ensuing blessing: «Who is good and does good, is not» required «by Torah law,» so the laborers working for the homeowner need not recite it. «Rav Ashi,» on the other hand, would «answer» amen «in a whisper, so that» those who heard him «would not relate to» the blessing: «Who is good and does good, with contempt.»

segments.he: רַבִּי זֵירָא חֲלַשׁ, עָל לְגַבֵּיהּ רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, קַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ: אִי מִתְּפַח קַטִּינָא חֲרִיךְ שָׁקֵי — עָבֵידְנָא יוֹמָא טָבָא לְרַבָּנַן. אִתְּפַח, עֲבַד סְעוֹדְתָּא לְכוּלְּהוּ רַבָּנַן. כִּי מְטָא לְמִשְׁרֵי אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי זֵירָא: לִישְׁרֵי לַן מָר. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּאָמַר: בַּעַל הַבַּיִת בּוֹצֵעַ? שְׁרָא לְהוּ.
segments.en: The Gemara recounts: «Rabbi Zeira took ill. Rabbi Abbahu went to visit him and resolved: If the little man with the scorched legs,» a nickname for Rabbi Zeira, «is cured, I will make a festival,» a feast, «for the Sages.» Rabbi Zeira «was cured and» Rabbi Abbahu «made a feast for all the Sages. When it came time to break» bread, Rabbi Abbahu «said to Rabbi Zeira: Master,» please «break» bread «for us.» Rabbi Zeira «said to him: Doesn’t the Master hold» in accordance with «that» halakha «of Rabbi Yoḥanan,» who «said: The host breaks» bread? Rabbi Abbahu «broke» bread «for them.»

segments.he: כִּי מְטָא לְבָרוֹכֵי, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נְבָרֵיךְ לַן מָר. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּרַב הוּנָא דְּמִן בָּבֶל דְּאָמַר: בּוֹצֵעַ מְבָרֵךְ?
segments.en: «When» the time «came to recite the blessing,» Rabbi Abbahu «said to» Rabbi Zeira: «Master, recite» Grace after Meals «on our behalf.» Rabbi Zeira «said to him: Doesn’t the Master hold» in accordance with «that» halakha «of Rabbi Huna of Babylonia,» who «said: He who breaks» bread «recites» Grace after Meals?

segments.he: וְאִיהוּ, כְּמַאן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ?
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And in accordance with whose» opinion «does» Rabbi Abbahu «hold» that he asked Rabbi Zeira to recite Grace after Meals?

segments.he: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי: בַּעַל הַבַּיִת בּוֹצֵעַ, וְאוֹרֵחַ מְבָרֵךְ. בַּעַל הַבַּיִת בּוֹצֵעַ — כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּבְצַע בְּעַיִן יָפָה. וְאוֹרֵחַ מְבָרֵךְ — כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּבָרֵךְ בַּעַל הַבַּיִת.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: Rabbi Abbahu holds in accordance with that halakha «that Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai: The host breaks bread and a guest recites» Grace after Meals. «The host breaks» bread «so that he will break» bread «generously,» whereas a guest might be embarrassed to break a large piece for himself and other guests; «and the guest recites» Grace after Meals «so that he may bless the host» in the course of reciting Grace after Meals, as the Gemara proceeds to explain.

segments.he: מַאי מְבָרֵךְ — ״יְהִי רָצוֹן שֶׁלֹּא יֵבוֹשׁ בַּעַל הַבַּיִת בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְלֹא יִכָּלֵם לְעוֹלָם הַבָּא״.
segments.en: «What is» the formula of the blessing with which the guest «blesses» his host? «May it be Your will that the master of the house shall not suffer shame in this world, nor humiliation in the World-to-Come.»

segments.he: וְרַבִּי מוֹסִיף בָּהּ דְּבָרִים: ״וְיִצְלַח מְאֹד בְּכָל נְכָסָיו, וְיִהְיוּ נְכָסָיו וּנְכָסֵינוּ מוּצְלָחִים וּקְרוֹבִים לָעִיר, וְאַל יִשְׁלוֹט שָׂטָן לֹא בְּמַעֲשֵׂי יָדָיו וְלֹא בְּמַעֲשֵׂי יָדֵינוּ, וְאַל יִזְדַּקֵּר לֹא לְפָנָיו וְלֹא לְפָנֵינוּ שׁוּם דְּבַר הִרְהוּר חֵטְא וַעֲבֵירָה וְעָוֹן מֵעַתָּה וְעַד עוֹלָם״.
segments.en: «Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «added to it elements» pertaining to material success: «And may he be very successful with all his possessions,» «and may his possessions and our possessions be successful and near the city,» «and may Satan control neither his deeds nor our deeds,» «and may no thought of sin, iniquity, or transgression stand before him or before us» «from now and for evermore.»

moves.summary: Brings the dispute of Rav and Rabbi Yoḥanan, extending the mishna's rule for three to a pair who wish to join.
moves.about: brings the unattributed amoraic dispute over whether two who ate together may opt into a zimmun

moves.summary: Objects from the mishna: three are required, so three yes and two no.
moves.target: unnamed:the amora who permits two who ate together to form a zimmun
moves.about: whether two may opt into a zimmun, given that the mishna imposes it only on three

moves.summary: Answers that the mishna speaks of an obligatory zimmun and the amoraim of an optional one.
moves.about: whether the mishna's rule for three bears at all on an optional zimmun of two

moves.summary: Objects from the teaching that three may not disperse — which would be harmless if two could still form a zimmun.
moves.target: unnamed:the amora who permits two who ate together to form a zimmun
moves.about: whether two may opt into a zimmun, given that three are forbidden to disperse

moves.cueHe: שאני התם דקבעו להו בחובה מעיקרא
moves.summary: Rejects the proof: those three had already fixed themselves in an obligation from the outset.
moves.about: whether the ban on dispersing proves anything about two who never were three

moves.summary: Objects from the baraita of the waiter, who joins two without permission but needs it to join three.
moves.target: unnamed:the amora who permits two who ate together to form a zimmun
moves.about: whether two may form a zimmun, given that a waiter serving two joins them without permission but serving three needs it

moves.summary: Answers that the pair prefer to be fixed in an obligation from the outset, so the waiter joins them uninvited.
moves.about: why the waiter joins two without permission — the pair prefer an obligatory zimmun from the outset

moves.summary: Objects the other way: women, reckoned as no more than two men, do form a zimmun for themselves.
moves.target: unnamed:the amora who forbids two who ate together to form a zimmun
moves.about: whether two men may form a zimmun, given that a hundred women — reckoned as only two men — form one for themselves

moves.summary: Rejects the proof: three women are three separate minds, which two men are not.
moves.about: whether women's self-zimmun proves that two men may form one

moves.summary: Presses the latter clause: women and slaves together are also separate minds, yet may not form a zimmun.
moves.about: whether three separate minds is the operative reason, given that the baraita's latter clause bars women and slaves together

moves.summary: Answers that the latter clause turns on promiscuity, not on any want of minds.
moves.about: why women and slaves may not form a zimmun together — promiscuity, not a want of minds

moves.summary: Floats that Rav is the one who forbade, since his ruling about the one who left implies two alone cannot.
moves.about: which of Rav and Rabbi Yoḥanan is the one who held that two may not form a zimmun

moves.cueHe: שאני התם דאיקבעו להו בחובה מעיקרא
moves.summary: Rejects the identification: there too the three had already been fixed in an obligation.
moves.about: whether Rav's ruling about the one who left proves that he forbade an optional zimmun of two

moves.cueHe: אלא תסתיים, דרבי יוחנן הוא דאמר
moves.summary: Floats instead that Rabbi Yoḥanan forbade, from Rabba bar bar Ḥana's report that one of two fulfills his duty with the other's blessing.
moves.about: which of Rav and Rabbi Yoḥanan is the one who held that two may not form a zimmun

moves.cueHe: והוינן בה: מאי קא משמע לן
moves.summary: Attacks that report as teaching nothing: a mishna already says one who heard without answering has discharged his duty.
moves.about: what Rabbi Yoḥanan's ruling teaches that a mishna has not already taught

moves.summary: Rabbi Zeira supplies what it adds — that no zimmun blessing passes between the two.
moves.about: what Rabbi Yoḥanan's ruling adds — that there is no zimmun blessing between two

moves.summary: Concludes that Rabbi Yoḥanan is the one who held two may not form a zimmun.
moves.about: brings the mishna that one who heard a blessing without responding has fulfilled his obligation

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רבא בר רב הונא לרב הונא: והא רבנן דאתו ממערבא
moves.summary: Rava bar Rav Huna sets the Westerners' permissive report against that conclusion — surely they had it from Rabbi Yoḥanan.
moves.about: whether Rabbi Yoḥanan can be the one who forbids, when the Sages who came from Eretz Yisrael report the permissive ruling

moves.summary: Rav Huna answers that they may have heard it from Rav before he went down to Babylonia.
moves.about: from whom the Westerners heard the permissive ruling — Rav, before he went down to Babylonia

moves.cueHe: אמר אביי: והוא דקרו ליה ועני
moves.summary: Abaye limits it to where they call him and he answers.
moves.about: in what case Rav's ruling holds — only where they call him and he answers

moves.summary: Returns to Rav's ruling about the one who went out to the marketplace, to treat it for its own sake.
moves.about: returns to Rav Dimi bar Yosef's report of Rav in order to examine it for its own sake

moves.cueHe: אמר מר זוטרא: ולא אמרן, אלא בשלשה
moves.summary: Mar Zutra limits Abaye's leniency to a zimmun of three; for ten the absent one must come.
moves.about: whether hearing and answering suffices also for a zimmun of ten, or only for one of three

moves.summary: Rav Ashi attacks: the reverse is more reasonable, since nine look like ten but two do not look like three.
moves.about: whether the reverse is more reasonable, since nine look like ten but two do not look like three

moves.summary: Rules practically like Mar Zutra against Rav Ashi's objection.
moves.about: whether a zimmun of ten may be formed before the absent one returns

moves.summary: Asks the reason for that ruling.
moves.about: why a zimmun of ten requires the absent one's actual return

moves.summary: Answers that the Name of Heaven is mentioned, and fewer than ten present is improper conduct.
moves.about: why ten must all be present — the Name of Heaven is mentioned, and fewer than ten is improper conduct

moves.summary: Abaye reports a tradition that it is a mitzva for two who ate together to separate.
moves.about: brings the baraita that it is a mitzva for two who ate together to separate

moves.summary: Supports Abaye from a baraita, which adds that this holds only where both can bless.
moves.about: whether two who ate together should separate and each bless for himself

moves.cueHe: אמר רבא: הא מילתא אמריתא אנא
moves.summary: Rava states, noting it was independently said in Rabbi Zeira's name, that one interrupts for two but two do not interrupt for one.
moves.about: whether one interrupts his meal for two but two do not interrupt for one

moves.cueHe: ולא? והא רב פפא אפסיק ליה
moves.summary: Sets Rav Pappa's conduct against Rava — he and one other did interrupt for his son.
moves.about: whether two really do not interrupt their meal for one, given Rav Pappa's conduct

moves.summary: Answers that Rav Pappa acted beyond the letter of the law.
moves.about: why Rav Pappa's conduct does not refute Rava — he acted beyond the letter of the law

moves.cueHe: יהודה בר מרימר ומר בר רב אשי ורב אחא מדיפתי כרכי ריפתא בהדי הדדי
moves.summary: Three sages of equal standing ate together, with none of them the obvious one to bless.
moves.about: the two ate bread together with Rav Aḥa of Difti, none of them greater than the others

moves.summary: They raise whether the mishna's obligation holds only where one of the three is a distinguished man.
moves.about: the two ate bread together with Mar bar Rav Ashi, none of them greater than the others

moves.summary: Acting on that reading, each of them blessed for himself.
moves.about: came before Mareimar with the other two to ask whether they had acted correctly

moves.summary: Mareimar rules that they discharged the blessing but not the zimmun.
moves.about: tells the three sages that they discharged the blessing but not the zimmun

moves.summary: He forecloses the remedy they might propose: there is no retroactive zimmun.
moves.about: whether they may now go back and form a zimmun after the fact

moves.cueHe: בא ומצאן כשהן מברכים, מהו אומר אחריהם
moves.summary: Asks what a latecomer who finds a company reciting the zimmun blessing should say.
moves.about: what a latecomer who finds a company reciting the zimmun blessing should say after them

moves.summary: Rav Zevid: he says 'Blessed and blessed'.
moves.about: what a latecomer who finds a company reciting the zimmun blessing should respond

moves.summary: Rav Pappa: he answers amen.
Dissolves the dispute: each speaks of a different point in the zimmun formula.
moves.about: whether Rav Zevid and Rav Pappa really disagree, or address a company at different points of the zimmun

moves.summary: Sets two baraitot against each other on whether answering amen after one's own blessing is praiseworthy or reprehensible.
moves.about: whether answering amen after one's own blessing is praiseworthy or reprehensible

moves.summary: Resolves them: praiseworthy after 'Who builds Jerusalem', reprehensible after the other blessings.
moves.about: which blessing the amen follows — 'Who builds Jerusalem' as against the other blessings

moves.summary: Abaye answered that amen aloud so workers would resume; Rav Ashi answered it quietly lest the next blessing be slighted.
moves.about: that Abaye answered amen aloud after 'Who builds Jerusalem' so the workers would hear and return to work

moves.cueHe: רבי זירא חלש, על לגביה רבי אבהו
moves.summary: Rabbi Abbahu visited the ailing Rabbi Zeira, vowed a feast for the Sages if he recovered, and made it.
moves.about: that Rabbi Abbahu vowed a feast for the Sages if Rabbi Zeira recovered, and made it when he did

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה לרבי זירא: לישרי לן מר
moves.summary: At the meal Rabbi Abbahu asks Rabbi Zeira to break bread.
moves.about: Rabbi Abbahu came in to the ailing Rabbi Zeira

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: לא סבר לה מר להא דרבי יוחנן
moves.summary: Rabbi Zeira declines by invoking Rabbi Yoḥanan: the host breaks bread.
moves.about: whether Rabbi Abbahu, as host, should not be the one to break bread

moves.summary: Rabbi Abbahu accepts and breaks bread himself.
moves.about: who breaks bread — Rabbi Abbahu accepted Rabbi Zeira's point and broke bread himself

moves.cueHe: כי מטא לברוכי, אמר ליה: נבריך לן מר
moves.summary: At Grace after Meals Rabbi Abbahu asks Rabbi Zeira to recite on their behalf.
moves.about: asks Rabbi Zeira to recite Grace after Meals on the company's behalf

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: לא סבר לה מר להא דרב הונא דמן בבל
moves.summary: Rabbi Zeira again declines, invoking Rav Huna of Babylonia: the one who breaks bread recites Grace.
moves.about: whether the one who broke bread should not be the one to recite Grace after Meals

moves.summary: Asks whose view Rabbi Abbahu was following in asking a non-breaker to bless.
moves.about: whose view Rabbi Abbahu follows in asking Rabbi Zeira, who did not break bread, to recite Grace after Meals

moves.cueHe: כי הא דאמר רבי יוחנן משום רבי שמעון בן יוחי
moves.summary: Answers: Rabbi Yoḥanan in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai — the host breaks bread and the guest blesses.
moves.about: adduces the ruling that the host breaks bread and the guest recites Grace, as the view Rabbi Abbahu follows

moves.summary: Asks what the guest's blessing of his host consists of.
moves.about: what the guest's blessing of his host consists of

moves.cueHe: יהי רצון שלא יבוש בעל הבית
moves.summary: Supplies the formula: may the host suffer no shame in this world nor humiliation in the next.
Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi adds clauses on the host's property, on Satan, and on sinful thoughts.
moves.about: brings Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's additional clauses to the guest's blessing of his host
